Hi Alex / Sam,

Thanks again for the time earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) What we heard
- Use case: semantic search + recommendations in Acme's docs portal; intent to migrate from your current embeddings provider (OpenMatch) to Redwood for lower cost and integrated reranker.
- Scale: ~12M docs, avg doc embedding size ~ 512 dims today, ingestion burst up to 100k docs/day during migration.
- SLAs: need predictable latency for online search queries (~<50ms per embedding lookup) and strict PII handling.

2) Technical notes / concerns you raised
- Vector dimension compatibility and whether we support 512 -> 1024 model family.
- Batching and throughput during migration to avoid hot-start spikes.
- Normalization differences between OpenMatch and Redwood embeddings and impact on reranker quality.
- Auth and networking: VPC peering option for private deployment but start on hosted API for POC.

3) Proposed immediate next steps
- Marissa (me) to send a short migration plan + SDK setup guide (attached).
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineering + our Dev Lead (Dev Patel) to go over batching, KV cache, and reranker integration.
- Run a small pilot: 100k documents, compare vector dims (512 vs 768) and normalization strategies; measure recall at K and reranker delta.

4) Ask of you
- Please confirm availability for the technical deep-dive next week (we suggested Wed/Thu morning PT).
- Share a sanitized sample of 5-10 docs (no PII) we can use for the pilot.

Attachments: Redwood_Embeddings_Migration_Plan (spreadsheet) and API authentication guide (pdf).

Thanks —

Thanks Alex — great, wed/thu mornings PT works.

Quick answers to your technical questions (summary):

- Vector variants: Redwood exposes model variants; we can return 512 or 768 dims depending on the model you choose. For the pilot we recommend trying 512 (to match current) and 768 as an experiment. No need to change indexing pipeline — we can surface a conversion plan in the migration spreadsheet.

- Normalization: We support both un-normalized and L2-normalized embeddings. By default our SDK returns raw embeddings and we provide a client helper to L2-normalize on encode. For online search, we suggest normalizing at encode time to maintain parity with OpenMatch. We'll include exact normalization code snippet in the API auth guide (attached).

- Auth & networking: Hosted API + API key is fine for POC. For production, Redwood Private supports VPC peering and IP allowlist; we'll include steps and required IP ranges in the migration plan.

I've attached the migration plan and the API auth guide (see attachments) and added a short pilot checklist in the sheet: sample size, metric definitions (recall@10, MRR, latency P95), and rollback criteria.

Dev — looping you in to propose times and a short agenda for the tech deep-dive. Agenda ideas: SDK auth flow, batching strategy (max batch size and concurrency), KV cache warmup during migration, reranker integration (structured outputs + tool-calling), and evaluation pipeline.

Marissa
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Embeddings migration: post-call recap & next steps

Hi Alex / Marissa,

Thanks for the context. A few technical bullets ahead of the deep-dive so we can use the session for architecture decisions rather than clarifications:

- SDK setup / auth: Our JS and Python SDKs support API key auth and OAuth for longer-term setups. For the POC, use API keys with short TTL and rotate keys via our Console. Sample code: SDK.encode(..., normalize=True) to get L2-normalized vectors client-side.

- Vector dims & reranker: If you index 512 today and try 768 for quality, expect ~1.5x storage increase. Our reranker operates on token-level scoring and accepts candidate lists; we recommend a hybrid approach: coarse retrieval with 512 vectors, then rerank candidates using the 768 model outputs in the reranker stage. This minimizes index size while giving quality gains.

- Batching & throughput: For ingestion, use batch sizes of 512-2048 depending on GPU type; our pipeline supports adaptive batching. During migration, use distributed workers with backpressure to avoid sudden spikes; we provide an ingestion script in the migration sheet.

- Normalization & compatibility: If OpenMatch uses strict L2 normalization, set normalize=True in SDK. We'll run an A/B on a small sample to confirm parity. If differences persist, we can apply post-hoc scaling factors — we'll capture that in the pilot evaluation.

- Structured output / tool calling (reranker): If you want structured metadata (e.g., doc_type, section) returned with reranker signals, Redwood supports function-style calls that return JSON-safe payloads. We'll demo this in the tech call.

Proposed tech deep-dive slots: Wed 20 Jan 10:00 PT or Thu 21 Jan 09:00 PT. Please confirm which works and we include 30 min of Q&A and a short runbook review.

Regards,
